macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks fell Thursday as yields rose and Walmart slumped
items.summary: U.S. stocks declined in the previous session, with the Dow down nearly 700 points, the S&P 500 off 0.9%, and the Nasdaq down 1% as Treasury yields resumed rising and oil prices advanced. Walmart fell 9% after reporting its smallest sales gain in more than six years, highlighting cautious consumer spending.

items.title: Wall Street futures and indices rebound Friday after Thursday’s selloff
items.summary: U.S. equity futures and major indexes were modestly higher Friday after the prior day’s sharp drop, with markets attempting to stabilize as bond yields eased slightly. Earlier updates showed the S&P 500, Dow, Nasdaq, and Russell 2000 all trading higher in premarket action.

items.title: Treasury buyback plan helps cap long-term yields, but bond-market concerns persist
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury said it would expand buybacks of longer-dated securities to at least $4 billion per operation, a move intended to reduce long-term borrowing costs. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also signaled the government could increase repurchases further, but some market strategists warned the intervention may not fully calm the market.
items.source: Reuters/Bloomberg via Investing.com and The Edge

items.title: Eurozone business activity hits its strongest pace since November
items.summary: Eurozone flash PMI data showed composite activity rising to 52.1 in August, above expectations and marking the fastest expansion since November. The report also pointed to stronger new orders, a recovery in exports, and easing price pressures.

items.title: Oil prices remain elevated on Iran-related geopolitical tensions
items.summary: Oil extended its weekly surge as the U.S. moved to intensify pressure on Iran, with Brent near the mid-$90s and WTI near the mid-$80s. Market coverage said President Trump called the effort an “Economic D-Day,” adding to broader risk aversion in equities.

items.title: Gold steadies as markets watch yields, the dollar, and Fed expectations
items.summary: Gold held steady and was on track for a third straight weekly gain as the dollar weakened and Treasury efforts to restrain long-term yields supported precious metals. Markets were also pricing a majority chance the Fed will hold rates unchanged in September.

items.title: China prepares new policies to support domestic demand
items.summary: China said it will roll out a new package of measures to expand domestic demand and strengthen economic growth momentum. The announcement adds to the global macro backdrop after recent concerns about slower growth in major economies.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Crypto market adds about $280B in 24 hours after historic short squeeze
items.summary: Cryptocurrency markets added an estimated $280 billion in value over the past day as a large wave of forced liquidations turned a Bitcoin rebound into a broad short squeeze. Short positions were hit heavily across the market, driving a sharp risk-on move in major tokens.

items.title: Bitcoin climbs to around $77K amid heavy short liquidations
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 7.9% in 24 hours to roughly $77,137, after reaching an intraday high near $79,320. CoinGlass data showed about $1.5 billion in total crypto liquidations, with short positions accounting for most of the damage.

items.title: Bitcoin breaks above $79K as institutional flows and regulatory optimism fuel rally
items.summary: Bitcoin jumped nearly 9% in a single day to cross $79,000, while Ethereum gained just over 5% and several large altcoins rallied even more strongly. The move was tied to institutional inflows and improving regulatory sentiment in the U.S.

items.title: Trump-backed regulatory push lifts crypto sentiment
items.summary: Market coverage said U.S. President Donald Trump urged Congress to pass the CLARITY Act, adding to regulatory optimism around the sector. The same reports said the bill remains stalled in the Senate over disagreements on DeFi, company rules, and ethics provisions.

items.title: XRP outperforms major tokens, gaining roughly 24% in 24 hours
items.summary: XRP emerged as the strongest performer among the top 100 cryptocurrencies in the latest market snapshot, trading around $1.26 after a 24% daily gain. BitPay also announced that XRP is now available through its wallet.

items.title: Ethereum lags Bitcoin but still posts solid gains
items.summary: Ethereum rose between about 5% and 6% over the past 24 hours in the strongest market snapshots, trading near $2,375 to $2,401. Despite the broad rally, ETH underperformed Bitcoin and some top altcoins.

items.title: Arbitrum upgrade adds optional compliance screening and higher contract limits
items.summary: Arbitrum’s latest ArbOS 61 upgrade introduces optional compliance screening, priority fees, and a larger Stylus contract size limit of 96 KB. The screening feature is off by default, but the update signals continued development of enterprise-oriented tooling.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation launches post-quantum research challenge
items.summary: The Ethereum Foundation announced a Better Codes Open Challenge focused on hash-based SNARKs and AI-assisted research. The initiative includes a $1 million Proximity Prize for selected winners.

items.title: Nevada approves Tesla robotaxi permits for Las Vegas
items.summary: Nevada regulators approved permits that could allow Tesla to deploy up to 5,000 robotaxis in the Las Vegas area over the next year, while Waymo and Uber were each approved for up to 1,000. The move marks a major step for autonomous vehicle expansion in the state.

items.title: Google rolls out new Google News features on Android
items.summary: Google is adding an embeddable “Preferred Sources” button, natural-language Discover controls, and customizable audio briefings in the Google News app on Android. The update is aimed at giving users more control over how news is surfaced and consumed.

items.title: Amazon expands Prime Air drone delivery plans
items.summary: Amazon said Prime Air drone delivery is set to reach nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of 2026, a roughly sixfold expansion from its current footprint. The rollout would significantly widen the company’s same-day delivery network.

items.title: TDK launches edge sensor with on-device computing
items.summary: TDK introduced an industrial sensor node that runs its processing on the device rather than sending data to the cloud. The company says the rugged edge sensor is designed for long battery life and industrial deployments.

items.title: Meta faces major U.S. trial over child safety allegations
items.summary: Meta is defending itself in California federal court against claims that its social media platforms harm children and teenagers. The case could have significant implications for how the company operates its Facebook and Instagram businesses.

items.title: Alibaba reports sharp profit drop as it boosts infrastructure spending
items.summary: Alibaba said quarterly profit fell 75% year over year to about $1.6 billion as it invested heavily in infrastructure. The company also reported 45% growth in its AI cloud and compute segment and 9% overall revenue growth.

items.title: Unitree public listing surges in Shanghai debut
items.summary: Chinese humanoid robot maker Unitree soared in its public trading debut on Shanghai’s STAR market after raising about $900 million. Shares were up as much as 629% intraday before closing up 460%.
